findings.title: Additional rpaths can bypass the bundled library
findings.message: Checking that the bundled-library rpath exists does not exclude other LC_RPATH entries. If an absolute build-directory or other external rpath precedes it, an executable referencing @rpath/libaccesskit.dylib can load an external library instead of the signed bundled copy. The dependency whitelist does not catch this because it checks the unresolved dependency token.
findings.suggestion: Parse all LC_RPATH entries and reject paths other than @executable_path/native, or rewrite the executable's AccessKit dependency to @executable_path/native/libaccesskit.dylib before signing.
findings.evidence:
paths=run(['otool','-l',str(executable)])
  if 'path @executable_path/native ' not in paths:raise ValueError('required application-relative library rpath missing')

findings.title: Optimization disables every evidence check
findings.message: All evidence validation uses assert statements, which Python removes when invoked with -O or with PYTHONOPTIMIZE enabled. In that mode this script can print its verification-success message even when lifecycle counts, queue state, and attachment ordering are incorrect.
findings.suggestion: Replace assertions throughout this verification script with explicit checks that raise an exception or exit nonzero on failure, so validation remains active under optimized Python.
findings.evidence:
assert before['has_marked']
assert all(all(state[k]==before[k] for k in keys) for state in p['refused_states'])

findings.title: Empty refusal evidence passes saturation verification
findings.message: all() returns True for an empty list, so saturation evidence containing no refused attempts passes this check. Having 256 outstanding entries only demonstrates a full queue; it does not demonstrate that a subsequent admission was refused without changing the input state.
findings.suggestion: Require a nonempty refused_states collection, or preferably the exact expected number of refused attempts, before comparing each recorded state. Use an explicit runtime check if replacing the script's assertions.
findings.evidence: assert all(all(state[k]==before[k] for k in keys) for state in p['refused_states'])

fix.before: assert all(all(state[k]==before[k] for k in keys) for state in p['refused_states'])
fix.after:
assert p['refused_states'], 'No refused admission states were recorded'
assert all(all(state[k]==before[k] for k in keys) for state in p['refused_states'])
